title: Incidence of sexual dysfunction associated with antidepressant agents: a prospective multicenter study of 1022 outpatients. Spanish Working Group for the Study of Psychotropic-Related Sexual Dysfunction
authors: Montejo AL, Llorca G, Izquierdo JA, Rico-Villademoros F
population: Spanish outpatients with previously normal sexual function treated with an antidepressant alone or with a benzodiazepine, interviewed with the Psychotropic-Related Sexual Dysfunction Questionnaire; open-label, without a placebo group
funder: not read: the article appeared in journal supplement 62 (suppl 3); the publisher page shows the abstract without a funding or disclosure statement.
result: With specific questioning, sexual dysfunction occurred in 604 of 1022 (59.1%): sertraline 100 of 159 (62.9%), fluoxetine 57.7%, paroxetine 70.7%, citalopram 72.7%, venlafaxine 67.3%, mirtazapine 24.4%, nefazodone 8%, moclobemide 3.9%. About 40% of patients showed low tolerance of their sexual dysfunction. Results read from the abstract.
